findings.text: Input force feedback ABI caps type identifiers at FF_MAX with value 0x7f, sizes the table as FF_CNT one larger, and aliases the concurrent effect ceiling FF_MAX_EFFECTS to FF_GAIN.

Submission queue entry carries request routing and execution controls plus memory references and completion linkage in a fixed-size descriptor with alternative interpretations selected by operation kind. It groups a small operation selector and submission modifiers with priority and target handle, alternate offset and command views, alternate address and socket option views, a length word, a large per-operation option overlay, an opaque completion token preserved to completion, packed buffer identity selectors and personality selector, alternate secondary handle and length views, and a trailing extension supporting attribute pointers, option values, or expanded command payload when wide entries are enabled.

Read write attribute protection described by io_uring_attr_pi groups control flags and tag with transfer extent plus location plus seed plus reserved space, enabled by IORING_RW_ATTR_FLAG_PI as a low single-bit selector.

Submission modifiers occupy distinct low bit positions for fixed-file addressing, drain serialization, soft and hard linkage, asynchronous execution, kernel buffer choice, and success-completion suppression, each exposed as a shifted mask derived from its bit index, such as IOSQE_FIXED_FILE, plus IORING_FILE_INDEX_ALLOC as all-ones for automatic slot allocation.

Ring creation modifiers are single-bit selectors spanning low positions through bit twenty, covering polling style, queue thread placement, completion sizing and clamping, sharing and disabled start, error-tolerant submission, cooperative and deferred completion processing, wide descriptor modes, single-submitter optimization, mapping and index array opt-outs, hybrid polling, mixed completion and submission widths, and queue rewind, including IORING_SETUP_SQE128 for wide submissions and IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL for polled completion.

Operation repertoire enumerates file, socket, synchronization, namespace, buffer-management, and control actions under a dense small-integer code beginning at no-operation and closed by a last marker for sizing and validation.

Per-operation option words use low single-bit selectors for command persistence, data-only synchronization, absolute and clock-selectable timeouts with update and multishot behaviors, fixed input for splice, polled and level and update modes, scoped cancellation by descriptor or cookie or opcode, poll-first and multishot and fixed-buffer and bundling and vectorization for messaging, high-bit zero-copy usage reporting, multishot and nonblocking acceptance, message-ring data versus descriptor transfer with skip and pass controls, close-on-exec suppression for installed descriptors, and no-operation test controls for result injection and file and buffer and completion-width handling, with SPLICE_F_FD_IN_FIXED at the top bit and IORING_NOTIF_USAGE_ZC_COPIED also at the top bit.

Completion entry returns the submitter cookie unchanged with signed outcome and flag word, optionally widened with trailing padding for double-size completions. Completion flags mark buffer identity presence with identifier shifted high, multishot continuation, socket nonempty, notification versus data, additional buffer chaining, skip handling, and wide-completion indication, such as IORING_CQE_F_BUFFER with shift IORING_CQE_BUFFER_SHIFT.

Queue offset descriptors expose shared head and tail positions, capacity mask and entry count, status and loss counters, and index or completion locations plus a user mapping address, separately for submission and completion sides with overflow and flag words differing by direction.

Shared ring mapping uses widely spaced 64-bit offsets for submission state, completion state, entry array, and buffer rings with shift and mask helpers. Completion eventfd control offers a disable bit via IORING_CQ_EVENTFD_DISABLED. Mapping includes IORING_OFF_SQ_RING. Submission flags include IORING_SQ_NEED_WAKEUP to signal wakeup need, completion overflow, and requested kernel entry.

Entry and creation ABI pairs wait and wakeup and extended-argument controls with a parameter block carrying queue depths, creation flags, thread placement and idle, feature report, shared-queue handle, reserved words, and embedded offset descriptors. Feature bits advertise wait suppression, single mapping, lossless completion, stable submission, current position and personality handling, fast and wide polling, nonfixed polling threads, extended arguments, native workers, resource tagging, skip support, linked files, registered rings, bundling, minimum timeout, and attribute protection.

Registration multiplexor covers resource attachment and replacement with tagging, event notification, capability probing and confinement, queue sharing and buffer rings, worker topology and polling, plus advanced memory, zero-copy, resize, query, and filtering controls, from IORING_REGISTER_USE_REGISTERED_RING as high-bit selector to IORING_REGISTER_BUFFERS as base operation, while worker typing distinguishes bound from unbound execution.

Resource management structures carry counts and sparse selectors with data and tag pointers for bulk registration, offset updates with optional tag and count variants, skip sentinel for file slots, probe reports with last operation and per-operation support flags, restriction entries pairing an opcode discriminator with small selectors, task-level restriction headers with flexible trailing arrays, clock selectors, clone descriptors with source and destination ranges, fixed buffer descriptors with address length and identity, and shared buffer rings overlaying tail state to conserve pages.

Provided-buffer and polling controls describe ring registration with address, capacity, group identity, mode flags, and drain threshold. Status queries keyed by group return head position. Ring mode selectors cover mapping versus increment. Busy-poll tuning carries timeout, preference, operation discriminator, and parameter covering dynamic, static, and inactive tracking plus identifier add and remove.

Confinement enumerates allowance of registration and submission opcodes with permitted versus mandatory modifier sets closed by a terminator, plus a timestamped-wait bit. Synchronous wait descriptors pair timespec and minimum delay with flags, signal mask reference and size, and padding, in both registered and direct argument forms.

Layout hazards include endian-sensitive poll-event width with a word-reversed wide variant, packed buffer selectors to satisfy legacy alignment, flexible trailing arrays requiring length checks, shared head tail counters subject to concurrent update, overflow and loss accounting, and high-bit sentinels overlapping ordinary flag space.

Submission and completion coordination follows a shared-memory protocol where the application advances tails and consumes heads while the kernel mirrors them, using mask and entry counts for wrap, need-wakeup and overflow and taskrun signals to request entry or report loss, creation parameters to fix sizes and features, and entry flags to combine waiting, waking, and extended timing in one call.
User-space header guard LINUX_IO_URING_H marks inclusion of the ring ABI definitions.
